title: How should you answer when an interviewer asks why consulting, and why their firm?
description: How to give specific, believable answers to the two motivation questions every consulting interviewer asks, with an example structure.
hook: These two questions sound simple, and that is exactly why so many answers sound the same. Interviewers have heard "I like solving problems" thousands of times. A good answer is specific, personal and shows you have done your homework.
body:
Why consulting?

Link it to your own story. A simple shape:

  1. What draws you: one or two things about the work, such as learning across industries or working on big decisions.
  2. Evidence from your past: a moment where you did something similar and loved it.
  3. Why now: where you are in your career and what you want to build next.

Why this firm?

  • Name people you spoke to and what struck you in those conversations.
  • Mention a practice area, industry or type of work the firm is known for that matches your interests.
  • Mention something about culture or development that you checked, not just read on a brochure.

An example

At university I led a project redesigning our hall's food waste process, and the part I loved most was turning messy data into a decision people agreed on. Consulting would let me do that across many industries early in my career. I'm especially drawn to your firm's healthcare work. When I spoke to Sam in your London office, she described a hospital operations project that sounded exactly like the kind of problem I want to work on.

Avoid

  • Answers that could apply to any firm.
  • Leading with money, prestige or exit opportunities.
  • Criticising other firms.

Sources

  • PrepLounge: EY-Parthenon interview (motivation questions)
